newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GOVT AGREES SPEED LIMIT RISE TO 130 KM/HR.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GOVT AGREES SPEED LIMIT RISE TO 130 KM/HR.

text.p: The Czech government agreed on Wednesday to raise the speed limit on four-lane motorways to 130 km (81 miles) per hour from the present 110 km, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said.

It rejected a proposal to lower the normal speed limit in towns to 50 km per hour from 60, but it agreed to rescind so-called "S Cards" identifying officials and selected members of the public who could drive as fast as they pleased.
Slower Czech speed limits on motorways have been in effect since the communist era when the vast majority of cars were low-powered Skodas and Russian-made Ladas.
Since the 1989 revolution and the turn to a market economy, the number of high-powered western cars on the roads has risen substantially, as have the number of accidents and deaths.
